text: "Nothing restrains the Lord from saving by many or by few."
explanation:
The Philistines had surrounded Benjamin on three sides with chariots and soldiers "as the sand which is on the seashore." Israel's people hid in caves and pits; some even defected. Saul's six hundred men followed him trembling. Then Jonathan said to his young armour-bearer, "Come, let us go over to the garrison… it may be that the Lord will work for us."

Two young men climbed up on hands and feet, and God sent panic through the whole Philistine camp; the enemy turned their swords on each other. The hiders came out of their caves, the defectors switched back, and "the Lord saved Israel that day." God was waiting for one person to step out in faith. The odds don't restrain Him.

text: Israel had to pay the Philistines to sharpen their own farm tools. Depend on the world, and the world sets the price.
explanation:
The Philistines kept the secret of ironwork to themselves "lest the Hebrews make swords or spears." So on the day of battle, only Saul and Jonathan had a sword. Everyone else had to go down to the enemy to have ploughshares and axes sharpened, at an exorbitant charge. Shame was added to humiliation.

The church means "called out ones." Whenever the church tries to imitate the world's ways to do God's work, it ends up as the tail rather than the head. God isn't against technology; the printing press was invented to print Bibles, and it spread the gospel of grace. But you can't carry God's presence on a Philistine cart. Look for His fingerprints.

text: Shamgar killed six hundred Philistines with an ox goad. "The words of the wise are like goads."
explanation:
Israel didn't need Philistine iron. Shamgar delivered them with a farmer's ox goad; David with a sling; Samson with a donkey's jawbone; Jael with a tent peg. The Hebrew for goad, malmad, comes from lamad, to teach; Scripture says "the words of the wise are like goads… given by one Shepherd."

Never despise a simple word spoken to your child at dinner, a gentle correction, a sentence of encouragement to your spouse. David never once said to his son Adonijah, "Why have you done so?" and that son grew up to rebel. When God leads you to speak, your simple words become weapons against everything trying to steal your family.

text: "Do all that is in your heart. Here I am, with you, according to your heart."
explanation:
That's what Jonathan's armour-bearer said when Jonathan proposed climbing up to the Philistine garrison. Later, Saul proposed chasing the Philistines by night, and his men replied flatly, "Do whatever seems good to you." Same kind of answer, but no heart in it.

People follow those whose heart they trust. Jonathan's heart was set on the Lord, and his companion wanted to be part of it. Whether you lead a team, a church or your own children, let them see your heart. Speak heart to heart, correct with love they can see, and you'll find people saying, "I'm with you."

text: The flesh will do anything except wait. That's why Saul lost his kingdom.
explanation:
Samuel told Saul to wait seven days at Gilgal for him to come and offer the sacrifice. As the days went by, Saul saw his men scattering and the Philistines gathering, so he offered the burnt offering himself. Just as he finished, Samuel arrived. "You have done foolishly… now your kingdom shall not continue."

Saul led by sight, and his people followed him trembling. Later David had the same number, six hundred men, and because he honoured the Lord, his men became mighty men. When pressure mounts, the flesh wants to do something, anything, fast. Faith can say, "Stand still, and see the salvation of the Lord."

text: "What is that in your hand?" "A rod." God starts with what you already have.
explanation:
Moses had only a dead stick, and with it God brought plagues on Egypt and parted the Red Sea. A widow with creditors coming for her sons said, "Your maidservant has nothing in the house but a jar of oil"; the Hebrew suggests a small flask. She poured it into every borrowed vessel, and it kept flowing until there were no vessels left. The supply stopped only when the containers ran out.

God doesn't ask for what you don't have. "I only teach Sunday school." "I only have a little." It isn't the size of what's in your hand that matters, but His blessing on it. Stop comparing yourself with others and hand Him what you have.

text: The Philistines came by the coastal shortcut. Israel entered through the Jordan. You came through death and resurrection.
explanation:
The Philistines didn't belong in the land; they came from Caphtor, likely Crete, by the coastal road. Israel entered by crossing the Jordan. Joshua set twelve stones in the riverbed and carried twelve from the riverbed to the far bank, a picture of dying with Christ and rising with Him.

When troubles surround you on every side, remember who you are. The part of you that was frustrated, temperamental and hostile to God was crucified with Christ. You stand on resurrection ground. "If anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation; old things have passed away." The enemy is a trespasser on land that's rightfully yours.
